name: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross
history: The feast keeps the anniversary of the dedication of the church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem in 335, built by Constantine over the place of the crucifixion and the tomb. Tradition holds that his mother, Saint Helena, had found the wood of the true cross there. The cross, once a gallows, is lifted up as the throne of Christ’s victory.
life: Eusebius records the building of Constantine’s basilica at Golgotha and its dedication in September 335. Later in that century the pilgrim Egeria described the great crowds who came for the anniversary, and the faithful filing past one by one to kiss the relic of the cross on Good Friday. The story that Helena discovered the cross, around 326, is told by writers of the late fourth century, among them Saint Ambrose. In 614 the Persians sacked Jerusalem and carried the relic away; the Emperor Heraclius recovered it and restored it to the city around 630, and this too came to be remembered on the feast. Exaltation means lifting up: Christ said that when He was lifted up from the earth He would draw all people to Himself. Eastern Christians keep the day with fasting and a solemn veneration of the cross.
prayer: We adore thee, O Christ, and we bless thee, because by thy holy cross thou hast redeemed the world.
prayerTo: Lord Jesus Christ, you were lifted up on the cross to draw all people to yourself. Through the prayers of Our Lady, who stood beside it, help me to embrace the crosses of my own life, to see in them a share in your love, and to glory in nothing but your cross, by which the world is redeemed. Amen.
penance: Abstain from meat today, as on a Friday, and pray the Stations of the Cross or spend a few quiet minutes before a crucifix.
meditation: When I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all to myself. Which cross in your life might be the place where Christ is drawing you closer?
